0.long_answer: The syndrome in question is a rare disorder characterized by genetic autosomal dominant inheritance with variable expression, primarily presenting with facial abnormalities and malformations of the extremities. It was first described in 1973 in an article published in The American Journal of Diseases of Children by Drs. Hermine Pashayan, Samuel Pruzansky, and Allen Putterman from the Abraham Lincoln School of Medicine at the University of Illinois in Chicago. The syndrome is also known as Pashayan–Pruzansky syndrome or blepharo-naso-facial syndrome. Furthermore, a subset of patients exhibiting similar features has been identified and is referred to as the cerebrofacioarticular syndrome, which is sometimes known as Van Maldergem syndrome or Van Maldergem–Wetzburger–Verloes syndrome.
